scope: Confirmed login/enrollment/status and lock/unlock phone evidence, plus Jon's subsequent physical confirmation that remote start and stop work. Those start/stop calls follow the working API Lab 0.3.3 implementation; no additional export was required. Placeholder identities only.

recipes.label: Login
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with access_token; keep only in memory and enforce expires_in

recipes.label: Vehicle enrollment
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with one active record in enrolledVehicleDetails; the same-session encoded-@ form failed C500
recipes.encoding: Use encodeURIComponent(username), then replace only %40 with @. Preserve encoding for all other delimiters.

recipes.label: Cached vehicle status
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with vehicleStatus; later cached timestamps advanced. dateTime still determines freshness.

recipes.label: Requested fresh vehicle status
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 response, identical to cached body and dateTime

recipes.label: Unlock
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with empty body and tmstid; user reports physical success. Sole recorded poll was PENDING, not terminal SUCCESS.

recipes.label: Lock
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with empty body and tmstid; subsequent poll SUCCESS and user reports physical success.

recipes.label: Lock/unlock transaction result
recipes.confirmed: HTTP 200 with nextPollingInterval, tid and status. Unlock poll PENDING; lock poll SUCCESS. Empty command bodies do not imply completion.

recipes.label: Remote start (Santa Fe Hybrid, generation 3)
recipes.confirmed: Jon reports physical success in the tester. This is a user confirmation, not a newly supplied transaction export.
recipes.important_body_mapping: The non-EV start body vin is the registration ID, while the vehicle header vin is the VIN.

recipes.label: Remote stop (Santa Fe Hybrid, generation 3)
recipes.confirmed: Jon reports physical success in the tester. This is a user confirmation, not a newly supplied transaction export.

tasker_constraints: Jon explicitly chose standalone Tasker and authorized saved credentials in ordinary Tasker variables; do not add an APK or local bridge dependency.
Distributed XML/source contains no personal credentials. Session tokens and transaction details remain volatile Java objects; no secret-bearing response body is copied into result variables.
Only the four confirmed controls are included. Horn/lights and automatic profiles remain excluded.
Preserve the earlier bridge project. Check actual imported action counts and runtime before claiming Tasker readiness.
Never resend a command with unknown outcome. Preserve its private pending marker across process loss and require physical acknowledgement when needed.
recipe_correction: Earlier derived documentation incorrectly named owners.hyundaiusa.com. The confirmed runtime and supplied requests consistently use api.telematics.hyundaiusa.com; runtime endpoints were not changed.
